messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a burst of spot GPU preempts in us-west1-a, ~4 nodes gone over the last 6m. Some model-serving pods got 503/timeout spikes. Thinking we need a graceful multi-AZ drain orchestration rather than brute-force drains. Anyone free to brainstorm a POC?
ken: ugh, saw the same. autoscaler + node-term-handler is racing, pods end up rescheduled into already-saturated nodes. :face_with_steam:
terminator-bot: Preemption notice: node/gpu-spot-usw1-a-xyz will be terminated in 120s (reason: maintenance).
alex: can we add a short eviction-delay that gates the drain across the pool? like a per-node annotation that delays cordon/drain for N secs while we shift traffic?
sam: yeah, plus respect PDBs and prefer graceful pod migration using taint/toleration + priority classes. Low-risk: stagger by AZ so we never drain >25% of active workers from any model pool.
maria: exact thoughts: 1) node-term-handler should annotate node with evacuate-pending=true and sequence-id for ordering. 2) a controller reads sequence & drains nodes in a rolling window across AZs. 3) controller enforces "max-drain-per-az" and checks capacity before issuing kubectl drain.
ken: sounds good. we should also integrate with kube-scheduler predicates to prefer nodes with free GPU memory for reschedules. otherwise reschedules cause OOM and more churn.
julie: cost tradeoff: we'll need a small warm-standby pool (cheap instances or ultra-low-util GPUs) to absorb reschedules. keeping X warm GPUs in each AZ increases monthly cost but reduces 503s. need numbers — maybe 5% of baseline?
alex: POC approach: add a lightweight CRD EvacuationPolicy { maxDrainPerAZ: 1, drainWindow: 90s, warmPoolSize: 2 } + controller. sample YAML we can iterate on:```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: EvacuationPolicy
metadata:
  name: spot-graceful
spec:
  maxDrainPerAZ: 1
  drainWindowSeconds: 90
  warmPoolPerAZ: 2
```
maria: controller will: - watch node-term-handler annotations - enqueue node with AZ tag - check available capacity (running pods + warmPool) - if safe, run drain with `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` - if not safe, delay and poke autoscaler for prewarm.
sam: suggestion: use a local batcher that groups near-simultaneous term notices and issues prioritized drains with small jitter so we avoid N->N storm. jitter=rand(0,20s).
ken: also add network sanity checks: we've seen network egress throttling cause reschedule hell. controller should verify node NIC throughput isn't saturated before allowing reschedule jumps. maybe check CNI metrics or recent pod tx/rx.
julie: ops question — how will Dedicated customers feel about warm pools? For private deployments, warm GPUs might need different RBAC / billing. We'll need opt-in flags.
maria: agreed. we'll make warmPool optional per cluster and annotate clusters with warmPool: enabled. cost calc: assume 2 warm GPUs per AZ for us-west1 (3 AZs) adds ~6 GPUs; at spot 30% cheaper but still non-trivial. I'll make a cost spreadsheet after POC.
alex: quick POC script (bash):```bash
# listen for node-term-handler annotations and enqueue
kubectl get nodes -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west1-a -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' | xargs -n1 -P4 -I{} sh -c '
  if kubectl get node {} -o json | jq -e '.metadata.annotations["node-term/evacuate"]' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "enqueue {}"
  fi
'
```
ken: we'll want integration tests: simulate 3 concurrent term notices across AZs, ensure controller keeps available capacity >= target and doesn't trigger more autoscaler churn.
sam: also validate with large batch GPT jobs (long-lived kernels) — streaming reconnects are ugly if sessions die. we should surface session migration hints to clients (retry-after).
maria: next steps: I'll draft the CRD + controller skeleton. Alex can hack the bash POC to prove ordering/jitter. Ken & Sam, can you build a small load test that simulates 500 concurrent inferences and watches 503s? Julie can run cost scenarios and privacy checklist for Dedicated.
julie: on it. I'll also draft an opt-in clause for private clusters and list KMS/audit concerns.
alex: +1. will push a branch `evac-poc/graceful-drain` by EOD with basic controller loop.
ken: I'll add autoscaler hooks — an API we can call to request prewarm+shed. maybe a simple HTTP endpoint on cluster-autoscaler that accepts prewarm requests.
maria: perfect. if we get POC working we can roll out alpha to a couple of low-traffic namespaces and measure error rates/cost delta. thanks all :rocket:
julie: :thumbsup:
